title: MAI Licensed Weights: Frontier Performance You Control – Microsoft AI
content:
More of what makes a company distinctive will live inside the AI models it runs. Businesses increasingly want to control those models: who can access them, how they’re adapted, what they cost to operate, and when they’re upgraded.
That’s why we’re introducing MAI Licensed Weights, giving organizations the ability to deploy and customize Microsoft AI models in their own Azure environments.
Models you control
MAI Licensed Weights brings Microsoft’s frontier AI models into your own Azure environment, where you can adapt them to your business and safely integrate your proprietary knowledge and expertise. Your data and adaptations remain yours, with Microsoft only using them to train its models with your express agreement.
As these models become embedded in your most important products and workflows, you retain control over how they’re deployed, who can access them, and when they’re upgraded. That means you can innovate at your own pace, without compromising the continuity your business depends on.
Frontier performance, built for your business
The best model for a business isn’t necessarily the largest or most powerful general-purpose model. It’s the one that delivers the best performance on the tasks that matter, at a cost that makes deploying AI at scale viable.
By adapting MAI models to their proprietary knowledge and workflows, customers are achieving frontier-level or better performance on specialized tasks, at a fraction of the cost.
AT&T used MAI models to analyze 5G networks. For standard tasks, MAI outperformed GPT-6.1 Sol at just 1/50th of the cost.1 For more complex tasks, it achieved frontier-level performance at a significantly lower cost.
Other customers have demonstrated similar results:
Woven by Toyota used MAI models to fix software code, producing ready-to-merge fixes in 44% of cases where its existing frontier models required human intervention, at less than one-tenth of the cost.2
Alaska Airlines improved the accuracy of aircraft maintenance report classification from 81% to 91%, outperforming leading frontier models at a fraction of the cost.3
These results show what becomes possible when companies combine Microsoft’s frontier AI research with their own expertise: better performance on the tasks that matter, at dramatically lower costs. As more of that expertise becomes embedded in AI models, the ability to control and evolve them becomes increasingly valuable.
Get started
MAI Licensed Weights is coming soon through our Frontier Company engagements. To learn more, contact your Microsoft account team.
About these results Results reflect customer-specific evaluations of models adapted for particular tasks. Performance and cost advantages vary by workload, model configuration, and evaluation methodology.
AT&T: Customized MAI Code 2 Flash and Code 2 evaluated on 5G network operations analytics, including comparisons with GPT-6.1 Sol.
Woven by Toyota: MAI Code 2 Flash fine-tuned on historical MISRA coding-standard fixes, compared with frontier models used in production.
Alaska Airlines: MAI Code 2 Flash evaluated on aircraft maintenance report classification, with accuracy improving from 81.2% to 91.1% following tuning. Qualified employees retain responsibility for final decisions.

report.summary: Microsoft launches MAI Licensed Weights, letting businesses deploy and customize frontier AI models in their own Azure environments with full control over data, access, and upgrades.
report.background: Enterprises increasingly want AI models that they can control: who accesses them, how they are adapted, what they cost, and when they are upgraded. Off-the-shelf APIs often limit customization and data control. Microsoft's MAI Licensed Weights responds by bringing frontier models into customers' Azure environments, allowing adaptation with proprietary knowledge while keeping data and adaptations owned by the customer. This reflects a broader industry shift toward fine-tuned, domain-specific models that outperform general models on specialized tasks at lower cost. Microsoft positions this as part of its Frontier Company engagements, targeting organizations that need both cutting-edge AI and operational control.
key_points: Control and ownership: MAI Licensed Weights lets organizations deploy Microsoft AI models in their own Azure environments. Customers can adapt models to their business and integrate proprietary knowledge. Their data and adaptations remain theirs, and Microsoft only uses them to train its models with express agreement. This gives control over deployment, access, and upgrade timing.

Performance at lower cost: Microsoft says customers achieve frontier-level or better performance on specialized tasks at a fraction of the cost. AT&T used MAI models for 5G network analysis; for standard tasks, MAI outperformed GPT-6.1 Sol at just 1/50th of the cost, and for complex tasks achieved frontier-level performance at significantly lower cost.

Customer proof points: Woven by Toyota used MAI models to fix software code, producing ready-to-merge fixes in 44% of cases where existing frontier models required human intervention, at less than one-tenth the cost. Alaska Airlines improved aircraft maintenance report classification accuracy from 81% to 91%, outperforming leading frontier models at a fraction of the cost.

Availability: MAI Licensed Weights is coming soon through Microsoft's Frontier Company engagements. Organizations interested in deploying and customizing these models should contact their Microsoft account team for more information.

Strategic value: As AI models become embedded in critical products and workflows, businesses want to innovate at their own pace without compromising continuity. Adapting models to proprietary knowledge and workflows delivers better performance on tasks that matter, making control and evolvability increasingly valuable.
report.impact: This move signals a shift from API-only access to licensed, customizable frontier models, giving enterprises more leverage over cost, data, and deployment. For the AI industry, it intensifies competition on customization and data sovereignty, pressuring providers to offer flexible licensing. Developers gain the ability to fine-tune models on proprietary data within Azure, but need Azure expertise and may face vendor lock-in considerations. Regular users benefit indirectly through more tailored, efficient, and potentially cheaper AI services, with stronger privacy guarantees since data stays in the customer's environment. The emphasis on specialized performance over raw model size could accelerate adoption in regulated industries and complex operational domains.
report.tools: To follow up, watch Microsoft's MAI model family and Azure AI Studio for deployment and customization. Azure Machine Learning supports fine-tuning and MLOps workflows. ONNX Runtime can help optimize and deploy models across environments. For open-source alternatives, explore Hugging Face Transformers, Llama 3, and Mistral for custom fine-tuning. Also monitor Microsoft's Frontier Company program updates for access details.
